residents.why: a D1/D2 dwelling, as the labourer_dwellings clause admits
residents.basis: HOUSED HERE BY THE DEAL, NOT RECORDED HERE (L352). This household was present in the town on 1 July 1835 and no source says where it slept; the roof is the invention and the people are not. Their card carries their evidence and is not touched by the seat.

persons.name: Margaret Hayes
persons.note: RECONSTRUCTED, NOT FOUND. No source names this woman. She exists because the population model says the town held women of this age in this division that the naming sources never printed, and the whole of what is claimed is that: a woman of this band, keeping her own house, drawn from the 1840 Chicago schedule and reproducible from the seed printed above. No figure is drawn (L1).

persons.name: Daniel Hayes
persons.note: RECONSTRUCTED, NOT FOUND, AND NOT CLAIMED AS KIN. This person is in the house and nothing says how. The population model places older children out of their parents' houses as apprentices and servants, and the head of this one is not old enough to be their parent, so the record says `household_member` and stops there rather than inventing a relation. A source naming this household retires them. No figure is drawn (L1).

residents.research_note: RECONSTRUCTED HOUSEHOLD — a drawn laundress, in the west division. NOBODY HERE IS NAMED BY ANY SOURCE. The 1840 Chicago schedule counts children under ten at 27% of the town and women of twenty to twenty-nine as its second-largest band; the 1835 layer the sources can name holds 15 women, because the rolls that name this town — a letter list, a voters' roll, a subscription — print men. That gap is the shape of the evidence and not a reading of the town, so the order book counts it bucket by bucket and this household is drawn against those counts. Every value on it carries the model row and the seed that redraws it, and a source naming a woman who kept her own house in this division retires the whole record. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1).

persons.name: E Toe Won Gote
persons.note: CARDED FROM THE BORDERLINE ROSTER'S R6 (T-1376, stage `underdocumented`). Enrolled at Chicago in 1832 in the company the Black Hawk War roll heads INDIAN, with no 1835 corroboration and no card. The licence is R3's — the same roll, the same year, the same page — and the twenty men of Kercheval's company the town already carries were re-admitted under it. The roll prints him as `E TOE WON GOTE`, company `INDIAN`, enrolled at `CHICAGO`. The research READ this name and WITHHELD it, and that refusal is not overturned: this record is a reconstruction of what the town looks like if the name is admitted at the limit of its own evidence, and it says so on its face. The reading, the source and the refusal stand at `civic:data/research/civic/records/blackhawk_war_1832_chicago.json#records/blackhawk_1832_024#0` in data/reconstruction/1835_borderline_roster.json. REVIEW REQUIRED: this card is a record of a Native person at Chicago in the three years of the removal, and AGENTS.md's standing constraint holds it for review by Native scholars or community organisations before any scene carrying it may be marked released. No figure is drawn (L1).

residents.research_note: WRITTEN BY tools/reconstruct_underdocumented.py (T-1376), the `native_and_metis` half of the `underdocumented` stage of the 1835 resident reconstruction programme, under the owner's ruling of 2026-09-17 recorded in AGENTS.md. This file is NOT research and is not a mint output: data/residents/households/ is re-derived by the mint writers and data/residents/index.json is derived from that directory, so a card written here lives beside the re-admissions and is overlaid onto the scene by tools/compile_scene.py. REVIEW REQUIRED AND TOUCHES REMOVAL, both true, for the subject this record is about: a Native man at Chicago in 1832, three years before the removal of the Potawatomi from this place, inside the project's first target year. The review AGENTS.md commits to has not been held; until it is, no scene carrying this card may be marked released. docs/RESEARCH/native_and_metis_1835.md lists every source read and what is still owed. docs/LIBERTIES.md carries the invention.
